the dipole is a robust solution for planetary magnetic fields.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transition from dipole to multipole-dominated dynamos is a continuous process and is related to the development of zonal flows.
the transition between the dipolar and multipole-dominated dynamos is a function of Ra, Pr, Ek and the initial magnetic field strength.
, in the turbulent regime, dynamo solutions can be multipolar or dipole-dominated depending on the initial field and that, in the Ekman regime, dipole-dominated dynamo solutions are always present.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamo bifurctions are not unique and depend on the initial conditions and the control parameters.

the nature of the transition from dipole to non-dipole dynamos is very sensitive to the initial field and the Ekman number, which is a consequence of the fact that the zonal flows are not a robust feature of the dynamo solution.
the dipole is the preferred solution at small magnetic Reynolds numbers, but that the dipole can be suppressed by increasing the magnetic Pr and/or the magnetic Reynolds numbers.
